glossary.Urinary tract: The kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra.
glossary.Ureters: The tubes carrying urine from each kidney to the bladder.
glossary.Contraceptive diaphragm: A dome-shaped barrier placed over the cervix, which raises UTI risk.
glossary.Catheter: A tube passed into the bladder to drain urine.
glossary.Urethral instrumentation: Passing any device up the urethra, such as a catheter or cystoscope.
glossary.Flank pain: Pain in the side of the body over the kidney.
glossary.Acute pyelonephritis: Sudden bacterial infection of the kidney, causing fever, rigors and loin pain.
glossary.Loin: The part of the back between the lowest rib and the pelvis, over the kidney.
glossary.Leucocytes: White blood cells; their presence in urine suggests infection.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.Renal parenchyma: The functional tissue of the kidney itself.
glossary.Contracted bladder: A small, scarred bladder that holds little urine.
glossary.MSU microscopy and culture: A midstream urine sample examined for cells and grown in the lab to identify bacteria and sensitivities.
glossary.Pulmonary fibrosis: Scarring of the lungs, a rare side effect of long-term nitrofurantoin.
glossary.Breastfeeding: Feeding a baby with breast milk; drugs passing into milk must be safe.
glossary.Creatinine: A muscle waste product used to measure kidney function; trimethoprim raises it without real kidney harm.
glossary.CKD: Chronic kidney disease: long-term, irreversible loss of kidney function.
glossary.Amoxicillin: A penicillin antibiotic, used for UTI in pregnancy if the organism is sensitive.
glossary.Sensitivities: Lab results showing which antibiotics kill the cultured bacteria.
glossary.Broad-spectrum: Active against a wide range of bacteria.
glossary.Prophylactic antibiotics: Antibiotics taken regularly to prevent infection rather than treat it.
glossary.Immunosuppressed: Having a weakened immune system from disease or drugs.
glossary.Ascending infection: Infection that travels up the urinary tract from the urethra.
glossary.Bowel flora: The normal bacteria living in the gut.
glossary.Periurethral: Around the opening of the urethra.
glossary.Urethra: The tube carrying urine from the bladder out of the body.
glossary.Gram-negative: Bacteria with a thin cell wall that stain pink on Gram stain, such as E. coli.
glossary.Nitrate: A dietary chemical that some bacteria convert into nitrite in urine.
glossary.Leukocyte esterase: An enzyme released by white cells, detected on dipstick as a sign of pyuria.
glossary.Cytokine: A signalling protein released by immune cells that drives inflammation and fever.
glossary.Host defences: The body's natural protections against infection.
glossary.Physiological: Normal for the body's state, not caused by disease.
glossary.Ureteric dilation: Widening of the ureters, which slows urine flow.
glossary.Progesterone: A pregnancy hormone that relaxes smooth muscle, including the ureters.
